applicabilityBasis.summary: Hylo hyUSD is a general dollar-stable base claim on onchain crypto-collateral pools, distinct from the yield-accruing eHYUSD receipt and xASSET risk tranches. Mint/redemption routing converts among USDC and volatile collateral using protocol prices, fees, reserve availability and pool conditions. The reviewed public disclosures do not identify a legal issuer obliged to redeem hyUSD for a fixed amount of national-currency monetary value, leaving the section 2(22) payment-stablecoin test unresolved.

genius.notes: Reviewed on 2026-10-07 for Hylo Solana hyUSD, mint 5YMkXAYccHSGnHn9nob9xEvv6Pvka9DZWH7nTbotTu9E. The token is a dollar-stable base across collateral pools, distinct from eHYUSD appreciating Earn Pool shares and xASSET leverage tranches. The USDC route has a 0.2% redemption fee and requires reserve availability and USDC par tolerance; volatile-pool redemptions have collateral-ratio-dependent fees and restrictions. These conversion mechanics do not establish a legal fixed-national-currency issuer obligation. Issuer entity, domicile and licensing context are omitted because public sources did not establish them. Smart-contract audits are not reserve attestations. Territorial legal terms remain unavailable: the homepage returned HTTP 429, and an isolated named browser attempt returned an unrelated target URL, so its content was discarded and the tab released. No categorical issuerless or DeFi exemption is asserted.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, the independently opened regulator implementation materials, Federal Register inventory, NYDFS tables, token disclosures and regulator-domain searches did not identify a qualifying public GENIUS approval, state qualification, named official application, registered foreign exception or GENIUS enforcement action for Hylo Solana hyUSD. Its legal token issuer remains unidentified. This is a bounded negative-evidence finding and does not establish the absence of confidential or unindexed filings. Ordinary licenses and proposed rules do not establish token-specific GENIUS authorization.
